item.title: Base Building in 99 Nights in the Forest — Walls, Traps and Layout
item.description:
A good base in 99 Nights in the Forest is a ring of defenses around a strong campfire, with storage inside and choke points outside.

The standard layout

  1. Campfire core — everything is built within its light radius.
  2. Wall ring — one layer early, two layers once the Ram starts appearing.
  3. Trap lanes — traps on the paths enemies use, not spread evenly.
  4. Storage inside — shelves and crates next to the fire, so defenders restock fast.

Walls: the basics

  • Walls stop the Deer’s minions and Cultists, but Ram charges through — keep a repair stack of wood.
  • Reinforce weak fence sections before the Ram picks a lane.
  • Gaps are fine for shooting; open lanes are not.

Traps

  • Line attack paths with traps rather than walling every meter.
  • Re-arm traps between nights — a spent trap is a hole in your defense.
  • Later traps (once unlocked at the bench) can handle the Bear; early traps mostly stall.

Shelves & crates

  • Shelves and crates are cheap storage that keeps food and materials safe and close.
  • A food buffer of several meals per player prevents starvation mid-siege.
  • Keep upgrade materials (wood) in a separate crate so builders don’t strip the food storage.

Night-watch rotation

  • One player guards while the other restocks — both moving at night is how bases get overrun.
  • Assign lanes before dusk: east/west or wall/trap duty.
  • Call out Ram charges early so the builder can react.

Common mistakes

Mistake Fix
Building too far from the fire Keep everything inside the light radius
One big perimeter Multiple small rings beat one huge ring
No repair stock Keep wood crate accessible from inside
All players fighting One watches the fire at all times

See also: Campfire Upgrades for what to level first, and Weapons & Tools for the loadouts that make defense work.

item.title: Campfire Upgrades in 99 Nights in the Forest — What to Level First
item.description:
The campfire is your light, heat and anchor. Upgrading it changes how safely your squad can play — and it gates content like the fishing chat code.

Why the campfire matters

  • Night survival — a brighter, higher-level fire keeps threats at bay and marks your safe zone.
  • Content unlocks — level 2 grants access to the fishing rod path, which enables the yay fishing chat code (2 Gems).
  • Base value — the fire area is where walls, traps, shelves and crates do their work; a weak fire makes a strong base pointless.

Upgrade priorities (framework order)

  1. Campfire to level 2 as soon as possible — fishing unlock and a much safer nights 5–6 window.
  2. Level 3+ before expanding the base — bigger defenses only pay off if the core is stable.
  3. Leave the very last levels for late-game — they cost heavy wood and materials that are better spent on weapons first.
⚠️ Note: Exact wood/material costs per campfire level change with balance patches — always verify the live numbers in-game before planning a big spend. This is the intended priority order, not a fixed price table.

Quick tips

  • Assign a dedicated fire-keeper in squads so upgrades aren’t forgotten mid-day.
  • Stock fire fuel / wood before dusk — running out at night is a run-ender.
  • The campfire upgrade path pairs with the Crafting Bench upgrades — do both, bench first.

item.title: First 10 Nights in 99 Nights in the Forest — Day-by-Day Route
item.description:
This is the route most new squads follow to get through the first 10 nights without wiping. Build by day, guard the fire by night.

Days 1–2 · Get established

  • Spend daylight chopping wood and gathering food to keep hunger up.
  • Craft a basic axe and spear.
  • At night: stay glued to the campfire. Never overextend in the dark.

Days 3–4 · Scale up

  • Once wood is stockpiled, push crafting bench upgrades first — they unlock better tools and recipes.
  • Faster tools compound every resource run afterwards.

Days 5–6 · Core priority

  • The campfire is your lifeline — level it whenever possible.
  • Level 2 campfire also unlocks the fishing chat code (yay fishing → 2 Gems).
  • Build shelves and crates, create a food buffer so nobody starves mid-siege.

Days 7–8 · Defenses

  • Night threats ramp up here.
  • Ring the campfire with walls, line attack paths with traps.
  • Split the night watch — one player guards while the other restocks.

Days 9–10 · Expand

  • With the base stable, explore systematically — food, weapons and light.
  • Mark clues toward the missing children to set up rescue runs and late-game content.

Route summary

Phase Days Focus
Establish 1–2 Wood, food, basic tools
Scale 3–4 Crafting bench upgrades
Core 5–6 Campfire levels, food buffer, fishing unlock
Defend 7–8 Walls, traps, watch rotation
Expand 9–10 Exploration, rescue prep

The exact day thresholds shift with squad size — bigger groups can push phases faster; solo players should extend the “Core” phase by a day or two.

item.title: How to Play 99 Nights in the Forest — Beginner's Guide
item.description:
99 Nights in the Forest is a co-op survival horror game on Roblox: by day you gather, craft and build; by night, creatures attack your campfire. Your run succeeds when you survive the nights, keep the fire burning, and rescue the missing children.

The core loop

Every day follows the same rhythm:

  1. Gather — chop wood, pick up food and materials around the map.
  2. Craft & upgrade — the crafting bench unlocks better tools; upgrades cost wood and materials.
  3. Prepare — upgrade the campfire, build walls and traps, stock food.
  4. Defend — survive the night. Keep the campfire bright; darkness is death.
  5. Repeat — each night is harder, and later nights push you further from base.

Your real objectives

  • Protect the campfire — it’s your light, your heat and your lifeline. If it goes out, the night goes very badly.
  • Rescue the missing children — exploration and clue-hunting across the map lead to rescues and the late-game content.
  • Survive 99 nights — the long game. Early nights are for learning; later nights (and Forest Rage hard mode) are the real test.

Survival basics for new players

Rule Why
Never wander at night without light The Deer and other threats hunt in darkness
Keep food stockpiled Hunger kills runs mid-siege
Upgrade the bench before hoarding Better tools multiply every resource run
Stay together after night 5 Pack attacks punish solo wanderers
Walls ≠ invincible Ram breaks walls; keep a repair stack of wood

What to do on your very first day

Chop wood until you have a basic axe and spear. Stay near the campfire at night. Don’t overextend — dying loses your carried materials.
